title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - Prompt Engineering. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Which set names the three core elements of an effective prompt?
options: A clear task, relevant context, and a specified output format
A model, a temperature, and a token limit
A channel, a user, and a data space
A version, an object, and a field
questions.explanation: An effective prompt clearly defines the task, provides relevant context, and specifies the expected output format, and those three elements are the ones the guidance names as core.

questions.question: A prompt repeats the same customer facts in three places and the output comes back inconsistent. Which best practice does this violate?
options: The reference-once principle
Chain-of-thought prompting
Few-shot prompting
Explicit output formatting
questions.explanation: The reference-once principle says to name each fact a single time, because restating the same data in one prompt can lead to unexpected or inconsistent results, and grounding should supply the rest.

questions.question: A team needs every generated email to match their house tone and structure. Which technique should the writer use?
options: Add a longer role description with more adjectives
Raise the model temperature for variety
Remove all constraints so the model can adapt
Provide a few worked input and output examples so the model mimics the format and tone
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting gives the model worked examples of the task, which is the technique for making it mimic a particular tone, structure, or style, whereas adjectives and looser constraints do not set the pattern.

questions.question: A downstream system parses the agent's output as JSON, but the prompt leaves the shape implicit and the parser keeps failing. Which technique fixes this?
options: Raising the model temperature
Stating the output shape explicitly in the prompt, such as a JSON object with named keys
Adding a longer role description
Removing all constraints so the model can adapt
questions.explanation: An explicit output shape is a contract the prompt must state, so naming the format, such as a JSON object with named keys, is what lets a downstream parser accept the response.

questions.question: A prompt tells the model to be brief and also to explain every detail in full. What is this anti-pattern?
options: Conflicting instructions that cancel each other out
Few-shot prompting
Chain-of-thought prompting
Reference-once grounding
questions.explanation: Asking for brevity and a full explanation in the same prompt creates conflicting instructions, which cancel each other out and leave the model to pick one arbitrarily.

questions.question: To be safe, a writer pastes every field on the record and the entire case history into the prompt. What is the problem?
options: The prompt is now too short to ground the answer
Grounding is not allowed on standard objects
The context becomes over-broad and repeated, which dilutes the signal, so only the facts the answer needs should be injected once
The output shape is now JSON instead of text
questions.explanation: Over-stuffing the prompt with a whole record and its history dilutes the signal and buries the relevant fact, so the better move is to inject the specific facts the answer needs and reference each once.

questions.question: Which Trust Layer feature keeps prompts and responses from being retained by third-party model providers and from being used to train their models?
options: Data masking
Zero data retention
Toxicity scoring
Secure data retrieval
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the agreement with the external partner providers that says they retain no data and train on none, while data masking hides sensitive values, toxicity scoring rates content, and secure data retrieval governs grounding.

questions.question: Which two methods does the Trust Layer use to identify sensitive data for masking?
options: Pattern-based and field-based detection
Manual tagging and user flags
Encryption and hashing
Apex triggers and validation rules
questions.explanation: Detection is pattern-based, using regex and context with machine learning for values such as names, and field-based, using the metadata on fields classified with Shield Platform Encryption or Data Classification.

questions.question: Where does the Trust Layer store prompts, responses, and trust signals for the audit trail?
options: Only in the Salesforce Shield field audit log
In the third-party model provider's account
In Data 360
In the browser session that ran the prompt
questions.explanation: Prompts, responses, and trust signals are logged and stored in Data 360, and reading them requires turning on generative AI data collection and storage and installing the report package.

questions.question: For an Agentforce agent, what is true of data masking for LLMs at the point where the prompt reaches the model?
options: It masks the agent prompt before the model sees it
It is disabled for agents, so you rely on grounding permissions and prompt design instead
It runs only when the agent uses a BYOLLM model
It is replaced by toxicity scoring for agents
questions.explanation: Data masking for LLMs is disabled for agents, so an agent prompt is not masked at the boundary and you depend on secure data retrieval and on keeping raw sensitive values out of the prompt.

questions.question: What does the Trust Layer do with the placeholder-to-value mapping it creates during masking?
options: It sends the mapping to the model as context
It stores the mapping permanently in the audit trail
It keeps the mapping only temporarily and uses it to demask the response
It discards the mapping immediately with no demasking
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer temporarily stores the relationship between the original entity and its placeholder and uses that stored mapping to put the real value back into the response, which is why the user still sees their own data.

questions.question: Zero data retention is best described as which of the following?
options: A per-agent setting an admin toggles on the agent record
A feature that stops Salesforce from logging anything
A guarantee that grounded data never leaves the org
The platform's standing agreement with external partner providers, so the provider retains nothing and trains on nothing
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is an agreement between Salesforce and external partner providers such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI that they retain no data and train on none, while Salesforce still stores prompts and responses in Data 360 for the audit trail.

questions.question: An admin wants to stop an entire model vendor's models from being used anywhere in the org, across agents, prompt templates, and APIs. What do they use?
options: Hide the configuration in AI Models
Turn off the model provider in Einstein Setup
Set the Agentforce model option
Add an available when filter to every action
questions.explanation: Turning off a model provider in Einstein Setup blocks that vendor's models org wide across agents, prompt templates, and APIs, while hiding a configuration only removes a model from Prompt Builder selection.

questions.question: An admin wants to keep a model available to the org but stop authors from selecting it in Prompt Builder. What do they use?
options: Hide the model configuration in AI Models, which shows it as Hidden and prefixed (Not Available)
Turn off the model provider
Delete the configuration from the Model Library
Set the org default model to that model
questions.explanation: Hiding a configuration in the AI Models Model Library leaves the model available to the org but makes it non-selectable in Prompt Builder, shown as Hidden with the (Not Available) prefix.

questions.question: Where is the org default model that the Agentforce reasoning engine uses set?
options: On each agent's General settings page
Only in Agent Script model_config
In Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup, under the model for Agentforce
In the Data 360 Model Library
questions.explanation: The org default for the reasoning engine is chosen in Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup under Select the Model for Agentforce, and it applies to all agents in the org.
